title: Tabletop Bot Arena
pitch: Drive a small toy robot against three readable local-AI opponents in a tabletop arena.
capabilities: Weapon joints, contact-based damage and AI
Polished match loop shared across screen and XR
rules: Select wedge, lifter or spinner preset. Fight one AI bot at a time; no robot CAD editor or multiplayer in this release.
Rounds last 90 simulation seconds. Win by ring-out, health depletion or declared score comparison. Weapon energy and impulses are bounded.
AI uses the same drive/weapon action interface and cannot teleport or bypass cooldowns. Damage uses filtered contact criteria with immunity windows.
content: One arena, three player presets, three opponent personalities, practice dummy and a three-round cup.
state: world snapshot and stable component ids
match clock, score and cup progress

actions.xr: Ray-operated virtual stick or gamepad; hands optional

rive.role: Garage helper, match announcer and animated faces on bots via tiny texture panels.

polish: Clear weapon telegraphs and opponent personality
Bots keep physics hulls independent of face animation
Contact feedback without forced XR shake; restart in one action
tests: AI and player are constrained by the same action validation.
Damage cannot repeat unboundedly during resting contact.
Spinner speed/energy capped at solver-safe values.
Closing one arena cannot stop another world.
Cup save preserves logical progress and live match snapshot semantics.
XR exit while driving releases input and returns to paused current match.
loop: collect player command and bounded AI decision
validate drive, weapon and self-right against cooldowns
apply impulses/motor targets to one Rapier world
step then resolve filtered damage/ring-out events
drive crew/face animations from committed state
save: Exact same-build match snapshot; portable cup/progress save also available as a clearly different document kind.
xr_presentation: The full match on a placed arena board; optional spectator orbit on desktop, direct viewing in XR. Do not physically move the arena while the match is active.
comfort: Seated tabletop controls; no mandatory crouching or locomotion. Reposition pauses and clears held controls.
scope: Original toy robots and branding. BattleBots-style is descriptive; do not bundle branded logos, show assets or copied robots.
documentKind: Exact same-build match snapshot; portable cup/progress save also available as a clearly different document kind.
